images.caption: Figure 2:Overview of TinyAstral.Stage 1: humans specify the rules and budget in advance. A master of frontier LLM agents reads trajectories of the frozen teacher acting through the harness (tools, feedback, memory, recovery) and proposes harness edits, which are accepted only if a paired A/B test on selection seeds passes a pre-registered statistical gate; model weights never change. Stage 2: after evolution ends, we freezeH∗H^{*}and collect teacher trajectories, including reasoning and recovery branches. These are mixed with offline real-robot supervision to train tiny students (0.8B–4B), which replace the teacher in the same harness. Evaluation covers three training domains and three unseen benchmarks, plus three closed-loop real-robot tasks on an SO-ARM101 arm.

Figure 3:TinyAstral-4B recovers on its own(original evaluation runs, final harnessH∗H^{*}; blue labels: zero-shot). Top two rows: closed loop on a real SO-ARM101 arm; middle two: training domains; bottom two: zero-shot. Cards: tool calls and returned codes verbatim from the logs; amber: the decisive step; bubbles: the student’s reasoning before it. More examples, including Guava and a distilled-vs-untrained comparison on one episode, are inFigs.4and5.
